bib.title: The FACTS Leaderboard: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Large Language Model Factuality

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: all 18 pages, 58,753 chars. I read the body in full (abstract, sections 1-7, Tables 1-11). I skimmed the contributions and references from about char 53,500 onward. No appendices with results. Extraction was clean; no embedded instructions.

SOURCE: "The FACTS Leaderboard: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Large Language Model Factuality", Aileen Cheng*, Alon Jacovi*, Amir Globerson* and ~60 co-authors (leads Connie Tao, Dipanjan Das, Lukas Haas, Sasha Goldshtein). Affiliations: Google DeepMind, Google Research, Google Cloud, Kaggle. arXiv 2512.10791v1, cs.CL, dated 2025-12-11/12. No venue stated, so preprint.

NOTE CHECK: grep "FACTS" in 07-evaluating-rag-and-grounding.md finds no FACTS Grounding citation. The only hits are the word "factuality" and SAFE. This paper contains FACTS Grounding v2, a successor to Jacovi et al. 2025 (v1). The prompts are the same as v1 and the judges are new.

CORE CLAIM: Factuality is several skills (grounding to a given document, parametric recall, search use, image-grounded answers). Google bundles four sub-benchmarks into one "FACTS Score", the mean of the four accuracies. Each sub-score is the mean of its public and private sets.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
1. Table 1 (p2), 15 proprietary API models, public+private sets, accuracy with 95% CI. Gemini 3 Pro scores 68.8 FACTS Score. Gemini 2.5 Pro 62.1 and GPT 5 61.8 follow. Claude 4.5 Opus is 51.3. The best model is under 69%.
2. Grounding v2 (Table 1). Gemini 2.5 Pro 74.2 ±2.0, GPT 5 69.6, Gemini 3 Pro 69.0, Claude 4.5 Opus 62.1 ±3.3, o3 36.2 ±2.2, o4 mini 29.3. Judges are Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-5. The score is the mean of the two judges' percent-accurate. A response counts as accurate only if every claim is grounded and the response is judged "eligible". The paper does not state n for Grounding; it says the prompts are the same as v1 and documents run up to 32k tokens.
3. Judge validation (Table 10, p15), held-out private set, N=320, class ratio 79:19, against human ratings. The chosen judges are bolded in the paper, though the extraction does not show which cells. gemini-2.5-flash with prompt v2 scores Macro-F1 65.33 and gpt-5-2025-08-07 with v2 scores 65.18. gemini-2.5-pro with v1 scores 64.87. v1 judges were gemini-1.5-pro (56.89 or 55.65 Macro-F1 depending on prompt), gpt-4o v1 59.73 and claude-3-5-sonnet v1 53.15. These Macro-F1 values are low in absolute terms; the gain is modest and the margins are small.
4. Parametric (Table 6, p10), 2104 questions (1052 public, 1052 private), closed-book, Gemini-2.5-Pro as sole judge with 3 sampled grades averaged. GPT-o3 has higher accuracy than GPT-5 (57.0 vs 55.7). GPT-5 hedges 13.3% against 1.9%, so it wins on attempted accuracy (64.3 vs 58.2) and F1 (59.7 vs 57.6). GPT-5 mini hedges 67.6%.
5. Search (Table 8, p12), 1884 questions (890 public, 994 private), Brave Search API, Gemini 2.0 Flash auto-rater. Gemini 3 Pro gets 83.8 accuracy with 3.39 average searches. GPT-5 gets 77.7 with 4.28.
Multimodal: ~1,500 questions (711 public, 811 private). Gemini 2.5 Pro is top at 46.9 accuracy. The rubric autorater has Macro-F1 72.3 (Coverage) and 78.2 (No-Contradiction).

QUOTES
- p15: "A model response is marked with a positive label ("accurate") if all the claims in the response are grounded in the contents of the prompt, or do not require grounding; the response is marked with a negative label ("not accurate") if at least one claim that bears information is deemed to be not grounded in the contents of the prompt."
- p15: "Metrics that are focused on evaluating the factuality of the generated text with respect to a context document can be "hacked" by ignoring user intent." (This introduces the ineligible-response filter, Table 11 on p16.)

LIMITS
- The paper reports no per-model Grounding table beyond Table 1 and no Grounding n.
- Single run per model is implied, and I saw no seeds or repeats beyond the 3 judge samples in Parametric.
- Judges are mostly Google models, and the paper concedes self-preference bias (Wataoka 2024). Gemini 2.5 Pro is the sole Parametric judge.
- Grounding judge validation is weak: Macro-F1 about 65 on N=320, with a skewed 79:19 class mix.
- Parametric questions were adversarially filtered against five open models, and the silver labels come from Gemini 2.5 Pro.
- Search results depend on one engine (Brave).
- The suite does not cover video, fast-changing information, or knowledge-base tool calls (conclusion, p16).
- The authors say a fine-grained analysis of question hardness (tail entities) is not done.
- The leaderboard is public/private split and run by Kaggle, so private results cannot be reproduced independently.
- Authors are Google; Gemini models top the table.

BUILDS ON: Jacovi et al. 2025 (FACTS Grounding v1); Wei et al. 2024 (SimpleQA-style grading, which the note already cites as SAFE, arXiv:2403.18802, adapted with an added "unknown" label); Wataoka et al. 2024 (judge self-preference); Kandpal et al. 2023 (tail entities); Honovich 2022, Rashkin 2023 and Tang 2024 for grounded factuality.

BEST-FIT NOTE SECTION: "Faithfulness: claim by claim", sub-section "Grounding tiers" (line 126). It adds an all-claims-grounded binary verdict, a two-judge average to cut self-preference, and an eligibility filter against short evasive answers. It also fits "Faithful is not correct" (line 151) by splitting grounding from parametric recall and search accuracy. The hedging versus attempted-accuracy result (o3 vs GPT-5) could be a one-line aside there.

FIGURE: none strong. Table 10 (p15, judge comparison) or Table 11 (p16, ineligible-response examples) are tables, not figures. Figure 4 (p14) is only a distribution of domains and tasks. Figure 2 (p6) is a sentence-level annotation UI for Multimodal; it is not relevant to RAG.
